content.value_statement: Accessibility defects create barriers and raise compliance risk for web teams. This skill guides WCAG 2.2 audits with test steps, evidence capture, and remediation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Provides WCAG 2.2 checklists organized by POUR principles.
Combines automated scan guidance with manual keyboard and screen reader checks.
Maps issues to WCAG criteria, severity, and remediation guidance.
Includes examples for labels, focus styles, color contrast, status messages, and keyboard controls.
Supports audit evidence, retesting notes, and residual risk documentation.
limitations: Does not provide legal advice, certification, or formal compliance guarantees.
Requires access to the target UI, source, or test environment.
Automated tools identify only part of accessibility risk.
Assistive technology behavior still needs human review with representative users.

use_cases.title: Audit a Product Flow
use_cases.description: Review a signup, checkout, or account flow against WCAG 2.2 and document defects.

use_cases.title: Prepare Engineering Fixes
use_cases.description: Translate accessibility findings into code-level remediation steps and retesting criteria.

use_cases.title: Build Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable audit trail for VPAT, Section 508, or internal governance work.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Page Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page against WCAG 2.2. List likely failures, manual checks, and quick fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Keyboard Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this interaction for keyboard access, focus order, and focus visibility. Provide fixes mapped to WCAG criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Remediation Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these accessibility findings into prioritized remediation tasks with severity, owner role, acceptance criteria, and retest steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Audit Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a WCAG 2.2 audit report for this product flow. Include methods, evidence, criteria, residual risk, and follow-up tests.

output_examples.input: A page has unlabeled email inputs and generic error text.
output: Finding: The form lacks clear labels and specific error identification.
Impact: Screen reader users may not know the field purpose or how to recover.
Fix: Add visible labels, connect errors to fields, and retest with keyboard and screen reader flows.

output_examples.input: A custom dropdown works only with pointer input.
output_examples.output: The report flags keyboard access and name, role, value problems. It recommends focus management, expected keys, and retesting with a keyboard.

output_examples.input: A design uses light gray body text on a white background.
output_examples.output: The result identifies likely contrast failure, explains impacted users, and recommends measurable contrast targets for normal and large text.

best_practices: Combine axe, Lighthouse, or WAVE results with manual keyboard and screen reader verification.
Record evidence, WCAG criteria, severity, and retest results for each issue.
Prefer native HTML before ARIA when implementing controls.
anti_patterns: Relying on automated scans as the only accessibility review.
Claiming legal compliance without qualified expert review.
Using color, icon shape, or visual position as the only instruction.

faq.question: Does this skill certify WCAG compliance?
faq.answer: No. It supports audits and remediation planning, but certification and legal conclusions require qualified expert review.

faq.question: Which WCAG version does it use?
faq.answer: It focuses on WCAG 2.2, with checklists for Level A and Level AA criteria.

faq.question: Can it replace automated scanners?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret scanner output and adds manual checks that scanners cannot complete.

faq.question: What tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references axe, Lighthouse, WAVE, WebAIM resources, pa11y, and common manual testing methods.

faq.question: Can developers use it for code fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes remediation patterns for labels, contrast, focus indicators, keyboard controls, and status messages.

faq.question: Does it support VPAT work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help organize evidence and residual risk, but a qualified reviewer should validate formal VPAT claims.
